turns.content: How do apparent V magnitude and absolute V magnitude relate to observed brightness? Include the 10-pc definition of absolute magnitude and the flux-addition rule for an unresolved pair; assume no extinction.
Derive a formula for the combined apparent magnitude of an unresolved pair from its two component fluxes.
An unresolved system at 5 pc has components with apparent V magnitudes 7 and 8. What is its combined apparent magnitude?

At 10 pc, calculate the observed combined magnitude for a pair with absolute magnitudes 7 and 8 and for a pair whose components both have absolute magnitude 7, using the flux-addition and 10-pc definitions above.
Compare only the systems whose observed magnitudes have been determined and identify the brightest.
For the equal-component pair at 10 pc, derive its combined magnitude directly from flux addition, treating the component absolute magnitudes as apparent magnitudes there.
Check that every comparison uses observed flux and the convention that a smaller magnitude is brighter.

Why is distance irrelevant once an apparent magnitude is supplied, and what additional observational assumptions determine whether a 10-pc absolute magnitude can be used directly as an observed magnitude?
Report the brightest system among the cases that can be compared from the supplied assumptions, together with its combined apparent V magnitude.
